get.description:
Retrieve addon information for the authenticated account.

This endpoint is used to get the current addon allocation associated with your account.
It returns the available addon quantities such as additional accounts, operators, storage, and Twitter/X addon.

Response:
- Returns the current addon allocation
- Includes account, operator, storage, and Twitter/X addon quantities

Retrieve a list of accounts associated with your workspace.

This endpoint returns all connected accounts including their platform, username, and current status.

Response:
- Returns an array of account objects
- Each account includes id, platform, username, and status

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page to return, starting from `1`. Accounts are sorted newest first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per page, for example `20`. The response says how many pages there are in `totalPages`.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Only return accounts of these platforms. Send each one as `types[]=facebook`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Matches the account name or username, case-insensitive.

get.description:
Retrieve account usage statistics across all connected platforms.

This endpoint is used to get the total number of connected accounts along with a breakdown per platform.
It is typically used for monitoring account usage and checking limits based on the current plan.

Response:
- Returns an object containing total accounts and count per platform
- Includes platform breakdown such as Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Threads, and LinkedIn
- Includes account limit information
- Includes operator, the same breakdown for the accounts assigned to the operator when called with an operator API key, otherwise null

Retrieve detailed information for a specific account.

Provide the account ID to get full details including profile information, platform data, and connection status.

Parameters:
- accountId (string) — The unique identifier of the account

Response:
- Returns a single account object
- Includes detailed information such as id, platform, username, status, and additional metadata

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: ID of the account, the `_id` from Get Account.

delete.description:
Remove a connected account from the system.

This endpoint is used to disconnect and delete an account from your workspace.
Once removed, the account will no longer be accessible and cannot be used for any operations such as fetching content, comments, or posting.

Parameters:
- accountId (string) — The unique identifier of the account

Response:
- No content is returned on success (204 No Content)

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: ID of the account, the `_id` from Get Account.

get.description:
Retrieve account statistics.

This endpoint is used to get aggregated statistics for all connected social media accounts.
It provides an overview of account activity and platform-specific metrics available within your workspace.

Response:
- Returns an object containing account statistics
- Includes metrics aggregated across connected platforms

Supported platforms: Instagram, Threads, TikTok and Pinterest.
Pinterest returns the profile counts, the summary of the last 30 days and its daily metrics (only the days Pinterest has finished counting).

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: ID of the account, the `_id` from Get Account.

put.description:
Update the accounts associated with a content automation.

This endpoint is used to modify the list of connected accounts that an automation applies to.
It allows adding or removing target accounts without changing the automation configuration itself.

Parameters:
- accountId (string) — The unique identifier of the automation

Response:
- No content is returned on success (204 No Content)

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: ID of the account, the `_id` from Get Account.

get.description:
Retrieve a list of comments stored in the system.

This endpoint is used to fetch comments that have been collected and stored in Repliz (previously known as queue).
It includes comments from various platforms that are ready for management, moderation, or automation.

Response:
- Returns an array of comment objects
- Each comment includes id, platform, content, status, and timestamp

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page to return, starting from `1`. Comments are sorted newest first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per page, for example `20`. The response says how many pages there are in `totalPages`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `pending` (not handled yet), `resolved` (replied to or handled), or `ignored`. Every status when left out.

parameters.name: accountIds
parameters.description: Only return items of these accounts, as `_id`s from Get Account. Send each one as `accountIds[]=ID`. All accounts when left out.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Matches the comment text, case-insensitive.

get.description:

It helps users discover music that is currently gaining engagement.

get.description:
Retrieve a list of scheduled posts.

This endpoint is used to fetch all scheduled content that will be published to connected platforms.
It includes information such as scheduled time, content type, and current status.

Response:
- Returns an array of schedule objects
- Each schedule includes id, platform, type, scheduled time, and status

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page to return, starting from `1`. Schedules are sorted by `scheduleAt`, the earliest first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per page, for example `20`. The response says how many pages there are in `totalPages`.

parameters.name: accountIds
parameters.description: Only return items of these accounts, as `_id`s from Get Account. Send each one as `accountIds[]=ID`. All accounts when left out.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `pending` (waiting for `scheduleAt`), `process` (being published), `success` (published), or `error` (failed, the reason is in `errorMessage`). Every status when left out.

parameters.name: fromDate
parameters.description: Only schedules with `scheduleAt` from this moment, as an ISO 8601 date and time. Used only together with `toDate`.

parameters.name: toDate
parameters.description: Only schedules with `scheduleAt` up to this moment, as an ISO 8601 date and time. Used only together with `fromDate`.

This endpoint is used to get information about the current storage usage, including the total number of files, used storage space, and remaining available capacity.

Response:
- Returns storage usage statistics
- Includes information such as total files, used storage, and storage limit

Retrieve a list of uploaded files.

This endpoint is used to fetch files stored in your storage.
It supports pagination and optional search by filename.

Parameters:
- page (number) — The page number to retrieve
- limit (number) — Number of files per page
- search (string, optional) — Search files by filename

Response:
- Returns an array of file objects
- Each file includes id, filename, size, mimetype, and upload information

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page to return, starting from `1`. Files are sorted newest first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per page, for example `20`. The response says how many pages there are in `totalPages`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Matches the file name, case-insensitive.

get.description:
Retrieve detailed information of a specific file.

This endpoint is used to fetch complete information about a stored file.

Parameters:
- fileId (string) — The unique identifier of the file

Response:
- Returns a single file object with detailed metadata

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: ID of the file, the `id` returned by Init File or the `_id` from Get File.

delete.description:
Delete a stored file.

This endpoint is used to permanently remove a file from storage.

Parameters:
- fileId (string) — The unique identifier of the file

Response:
- No content is returned on success (204 No Content)

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: ID of the file, the `id` returned by Init File or the `_id` from Get File.

post.description:
Initialize a file upload.

This endpoint is used before uploading a file to storage.
Provide the filename, file size, and MIME type to create an upload session.

Body:
- filename (string) — Name of the file
- size (number) — File size in bytes
- mimetype (string) — MIME type of the file

Response:
- Returns upload session information
- Includes the file identifier and upload URL required to upload the file

Complete a file upload.

This endpoint is used after the file has been successfully uploaded to storage.
It finalizes the upload process and makes the file available for use.

Parameters:
- fileId (string) — The unique identifier of the uploaded file

Response:
- No content is returned on success (204 No Content)

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: ID of the file, the `id` returned by Init File or the `_id` from Get File.

delete.description:
Delete multiple files.

This endpoint is used to remove multiple files at once so they will not be executed.

Parameters:
- fileIds (string[]) — Array of file identifiers to be removed

Response:
- No content is returned on success (204 No Content)

parameters.name: fileIds
parameters.description: IDs of the files to remove, at least one, sent as `fileIds[]=ID`.

info.description:
Repliz Public API allows developers to securely access and integrate core features such as comment management, automation, analytics, and AI-powered interactions into their own applications.
This API is designed for external usage, enabling seamless communication with Repliz services in a scalable and efficient way.

Authentication
All requests to the Public API must be authenticated using HTTP Basic Auth.

- Access Key is used as the username
- Secret Key is used as the password

Example:
Authorization: Basic base64(accessKey:secretKey).

Make sure to keep your credentials secure and do not expose them in client-side applications. All endpoints require authentication unless stated otherwise.

token.description: Session token returned by Create Session Telegram, after Get Session Telegram reports `isConnected: true`. On reconnect the same Telegram account has to scan the QR code, or the call returns `400`.

code.description: The `code` query parameter from the URL Pinterest redirected the user to. It works only once and expires soon, so send it right away. On reconnect the user has to sign in with the same Pinterest account, or the call returns `400`.

filename.description: Name of the file, with its extension, for example `repliz-demo.mp4`. It becomes the last part of the file URL and is what Get File searches.

size.description: Size of the file in bytes. It has to fit in the free space from Get Statistic, or the call returns `402`. The real size is read again by Complete File.

mimetype.description: MIME type of the file, for example `video/mp4` or `image/png`. Send the same value as the `Content-Type` header of the upload.
